search_question_library: Search the published question library. Returns question definitions only - never response data.
list_questions: List the question library with each question's latest version and its status, draft and deprecated versions included. Definitions only, never response data.
read_question: Read one question: its versions with their statuses, and the complete definition of the version you name (label, help, type, required, constraints, messages and options). Authoring content only.
read_form: Read one form: its slug and title, whether it has a draft, its latest published version, what is released in the current environment, its steps with their question counts, its rule ids, the question versions its draft pins unpublished, and the COMPLETE working draft under `definition`. Start any form.saveDraft from that definition: a draft save replaces the draft wholesale, so anything you leave out is dropped.
list_form_versions: List one form's published versions, each with when it was published, which environments it is released in, and its step and question counts.
list_releases: Report this deployment's environments, which version of one form stands in each and whether it is closed, plus that form's release history with who released and who approved.
propose_questions: Stage new question definitions for the apply-draft card, and nothing else. It creates nothing: the definitions are kept only by an apply-draft card proposed in the same turn, and are discarded otherwise. To create a question the user keeps, propose a question.create step instead.
propose_draft: Propose the complete draft FormDefinition for the form this builder screen is about. Returns the advisory validation issues that would block a publish, and the warnings that would not. It saves nothing: follow it with the apply-draft action, which is the only thing that keeps it. It exists on the form builder alone; elsewhere, save a draft with a form.saveDraft step instead.
validate_draft: Run the publish validation over the draft you have proposed this turn, or over the form's saved draft when you have proposed none, and return its blocking issues and its non-blocking warnings.
project_draft: Project a form's draft for hypothetical answers and return which steps and questions a respondent would see. Reads no submitted answer. A draft with blocking issues cannot be projected: the result says so and names them.
test_rule: Evaluate one of a form's rules against hypothetical answers and report whether its condition matched. Reads no submitted answer and changes nothing.
diff_form_versions: Compare two published versions of a form, or one of them against its working draft (null), and report which steps, pinned questions and rules differ. A side that does not exist is MISSING, not empty: `outcome` is then `unavailable`, `fromFound` or `toFound` says which side is absent, and every comparison field is null. A form with no working draft comes back that way, so never read it as a draft that has been emptied. Structure only: no authored text and no response data.
count_links: Count a form's secure links by state in the current environment. No link URL or token exists to return.
list_links: List a form's secure links in the current environment with each one's state, whether it is single-use and when it expires. No link URL or token exists to return.
list_responses: List a form's responses under the response list's own four filters, metadata only: session id, times, version, access mode and flag state. Never an answer value.
count_responses: Count a form's responses under the response list's own four filters. Never an answer value.
delivery_status: Report a form's webhook endpoints and the state of their recent deliveries: counts by state and the attempt bound that was scanned. Never a payload, a consumer response body or an error string.
list_webhooks: List a form's webhook endpoints in the current environment and their recent deliveries with each one's state, attempts and last HTTP status. Never a payload, a consumer response body or an error string.
count_dead_letters: Count the dead-letter queue, by form, within the bound it scanned. Never a payload.
list_erasures: List the erasure log for the current environment: which session was erased, from which form and version, when and why. The log holds no answers.
diff_question_versions: Compare two versions of a question and report which members of the definition differ, by name. The names only, never their content. A version that does not exist is MISSING, not identical and not unchanged: `outcome` is then `unavailable`, `fromFound` or `toFound` says which side is absent, and `identical` and `changedFields` are null. An empty `changedFields` means the two versions were compared and nothing differs, which only ever happens when both sides exist.
search_forms: Search the forms this caller may read, by slug or id, and report each one's latest and released version in the current environment.
list_workspaces: List the workspaces this caller administers, with whether each is the shared library and whether it requires a second approver for a production release.
read_workspace: Read one workspace's members with their roles, and its access groups with the role, environments and forms each group grants.
propose_action: Propose one action for the user to review and confirm. It runs nothing: the user sees a card with every argument in full and confirms it on the screen's own control. Returns whether the proposal was accepted, or the reason it was refused.
propose_plan: Propose an ordered plan of actions for the user to review and confirm once. It runs nothing. An argument may reference an earlier step's result as { fromStep, field }, at most one such reference per step. The plan stops at the first failure. Returns whether the proposal was accepted, or the reason it was refused.
